titulo: The dish you were not going to order
subtitulo: Taverna, estiatório, ouzerí, psistariá — four words that are an expectation about the menu, not an official category
cena: A laminated menu with photographs on it in one hand, and a woman two tables away eating something that is not on it.
frasePiso: Ask what they have today. That list is shorter than the menu, and it is the one worth ordering from.
decisao: which dish you order, and for how much — whether you ask what they have today and name the magireftá, or pick off the laminated card at the laminated card's prices

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Taverna, estiatório, ouzerí and psistariá are not legal categories. Greek food-safety law groups all of them together as επιχειρήσεις μαζικής εστίασης, under the notification regime of law 4442/2016. The distinction between them is commercial and customary — an expectation about the menu and the register of the room, not an official classification.
fatosDatados.fonte: ν.4442/2016, regime de γνωστοποίηση; a legislação sanitária agrupa os estabelecimentos em «επιχειρήσεις μαζικής εστίασης» — a distinção entre ταβέρνα, εστιατόριο, ουζερί e ψησταριά é comercial e consuetudinária, não legal

fatosDatados.afirmacao: A cover charge is prohibited in Greece. Article 72 of the ΔΙ.Ε.Π.Π.Υ. rules bars κουβέρ, and no product — bread and bottled water included — may be served and charged without prior consent, with a fine of €500 per item. Bread may be charged as an item if it is offered and accepted.
fatosDatados.fonte: Art. 72 dos Κανόνες ΔΙ.Ε.Π.Π.Υ., ΥΑ 91354/2017, ΦΕΚ Β΄2983/30.8.2017 — proibição de κουβέρ e de servir e cobrar qualquer produto sem consentimento prévio; multa de €500 por item

fatosDatados.afirmacao: The Mediterranean Diet is inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, file ICH 00884, with Greece among the submitting states. The inscription states verbatim: «Eating together is the foundation of the cultural identity and continuity of communities throughout the Mediterranean basin.»
fatosDatados.fonte: UNESCO, Lista Representativa do Património Cultural Imaterial da Humanidade, ficha ICH 00884 — Dieta Mediterrânea, Grécia entre os proponentes

steps.pt: Four words on four signs: taverna, estiatório, ouzerí, psistariá. None of them is an official category.
The law files them all together. What the four words carry is an expectation about the menu and the room.

steps.promptPt: The laminated menu has forty things on it and you want the short list instead. Speak now.
steps.pt: What have you got today?
We have pot dishes and things grilled to order.
steps.acao: Two families, and he just named both. Magireftá were cooked this morning; tis óras goes on the grill now.

steps.pt: The frame from part six comes back. Éhete, then the thing — and here the thing is what is cooking today.

steps.promptPt: You want the tray dishes that were made this morning, not something off the grill. Ask for them by name. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have pot dishes?
Today we have stuffed vegetables and briám.
steps.acao: Two names, said fast. Do not translate them — repeat one of them back and it becomes your order.

steps.promptPt: He named two things and you recognised neither. Get one of them explained instead of retreating to the menu. Speak now.
steps.pt: What is that?

steps.promptPt: There is a glass counter by the till with today's trays in it. Ask before you lean over. Speak now.
steps.pt: May I have a look?
Mezédes are small plates that arrive for the table. Ordering a few of them is ordering for everybody at once.

steps.promptPt: Three of you, nobody sure what they want, and one decision would solve it. Speak now.
steps.pt: We'll take a few small plates.

steps.promptPt: He has been doing this for thirty years and you have been reading a menu for two minutes. Hand it over. Speak now.
steps.pt: What do you recommend for us?
A cover charge is illegal here, and nothing may be served and charged unless you agreed to it first.
The bread is charged. Do you want it?
steps.acao: That question is the rule working. Answer it either way, and the answer is the whole of your consent.

steps.pt: Bread and bottled water are covered too. If either arrives unasked, you can say no without any fuss.

steps.promptPt: A basket lands on the table and you did not ask for it and do not want it. One calm sentence. Speak now.
steps.pt: No bread, thank you.

steps.promptPt: Someone at your table does not eat meat and the day's list was read out loud, not printed. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have anything without meat?

steps.promptPt: The wine list is three imported labels and there is a barrel behind the counter. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have local wine?
Shall I bring it all together?
steps.acao: He is asking about order of arrival, not about quantity. Yes means the table fills at once.

steps.promptPt: You have decided, it is one of the two he named, and you can point at the tray. Speak now.
steps.pt: I'll have that one.

steps.promptPt: The dish they brought was the best thing you have eaten here. Tell them, and ask what else they do like that. Speak now.
steps.es: Ήταν πεντανόστιμο! Τι άλλο κάνετε καλά;
steps.pinyin: EE-tan pen-da-NO-sti-mo! tee AL-lo KA-ne-te ka-LA
steps.pt: That was delicious! What else do you do well?
steps.tts: Ήταν πεντανόστιμο! Τι άλλο κάνετε καλά;

steps.pt: Mporó na do is a sentence, not a licence. It asks to look at what is out, not to walk into a kitchen.

steps.es: Τι έχετε σήμερα; Έχετε μαγειρευτά; Τι μας προτείνετε;
steps.pinyin: ti E-he-te SI-me-ra · E-he-te ma-yi-ref-TA · ti mas pro-TI-ne-te
steps.pt: Shadow the three questions that get you off the laminated menu and onto today's list.
steps.tts: Τι έχετε σήμερα; Έχετε μαγειρευτά; Τι μας προτείνετε;

steps.pt: I03 done. What is cooking today, magireftá by name, and the bread you agree to before it is charged.

aprofundar.titulo: Four words, two families and one question

secoes.titulo: The four words are custom, not law
secoes.corpo: Greek food-safety law does not know what a taverna is. It files taverna, estiatório, ouzerí and psistariá together as επιχειρήσεις μαζικής εστίασης under the notification regime of law 4442/2016. The four words are a commercial and customary distinction, and that is exactly what makes them useful: they tell you what to expect on the menu and what register the room is in, and they promise nothing beyond that. A tsipourádiko is mostly a Vólos and Thessaly thing, so treat that one as regional rather than national.

Magireftá are the dishes cooked earlier in trays and pots — stuffed vegetables, beans, briám, things that sat and got better. Tis óras is what goes on the grill when you order it. Asking éhete magireftá names a whole family in two words, and it is the family a laminated tourist menu tends to bury.

secoes.titulo: Bread, water and the thing that cannot be charged
secoes.corpo: Cover charge is prohibited outright, and no product at all — bread and bottled water explicitly included — may be served and charged without prior consent, at €500 an item. Bread can perfectly well appear on the bill if it was offered and you said yes. So the question to listen for is thélete, and the useful answer is whichever one you actually mean.

Mezédes are small plates that come to the middle of the table, so ordering a few of them settles what everybody eats in one sentence instead of four. That is a fact about how the plates arrive, and it is the whole of the claim this course makes. Separately, and it proves nothing about your table: UNESCO's inscription of the Mediterranean Diet, which Greece helped submit, records that eating together is foundational to the identity and continuity of communities across the Mediterranean. That is heritage listing, not an anthropological rule about who shares what — do not read it as one.

You will read in a lot of travel writing that visitors go into Greek kitchens to look in the pots. This course does not make that claim: there is no source behind it. What the course gives you is the sentence — mporó na do, may I have a look — which is ordinary, polite, and answerable with a yes or a no by whoever is standing there.

permissao: You are allowed to ignore the menu in your hand. The laminated card with pictures is not the enemy and it is not a trap — it is just a slower document than the person standing next to you, who knows what came out of the oven at eleven this morning and will tell you if you ask.
espelho: Anyone who has eaten in their own city and watched a visitor order the one dish on the menu that exists purely for visitors knows this from the other side. It is never that the visitor was fooled — it is that nobody asked, and the short list is only ever spoken out loud.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You are choosing between two places by the word on the sign — taverna here, estiatório there — and treating it as a grading.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: One of these words means the authentic one and the other means the tourist one.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The words are not legal categories: food-safety law groups all of them as mass catering businesses under a single notification regime. The distinction is commercial and customary, so it tells you what kind of menu and what register of room to expect, and nothing about who eats there.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Stop grading by the sign and ask inside instead: ti éhete símera, and éhete magireftá. The answer sorts the room in one sentence.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop paying for a word on an awning and start choosing by what is actually cooked in the building.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a claim that the words are meaningless — they are a real and useful expectation. And glosses vary by region: a tsipourádiko is largely a Vólos and Thessaly institution, not a national one.

fichasCulturais.sinal: Bread you did not order arrives at the table, and a small charge for it turns up on the bill.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: This is the local version of a cover charge and arguing about it would be tedious.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Cover charge is prohibited, and no product — bread and bottled water named explicitly — may be served and charged without prior consent, with a €500 fine per item. Bread offered and accepted is a normal chargeable item; bread landed silently and billed is not.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Listen for thélete when it arrives, and answer it. If it comes without a question and you do not want it, óhi psomí, efharistó is enough, said once and calmly.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop bracing for a charge that is not supposed to be there, and you keep the exchange friendly because you handled it at the table rather than at the bill.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a rule that bread is free — offered and accepted, it is a legitimate item at a legitimate price. And this is a consumer rule to know, not a script for a confrontation over one euro.
